name: Battle of Cannae
note: The Carthaginian left lay to the south by the Aufidus and the Romans faced east, so north is drawn at the top. The day falls on 2 August 216 BCE by the Roman calendar and on 1 July by one modern reckoning, so no date is shown. Varro held the Roman left and Paullus the right by the usual telling, though Samuels doubted who commanded where. Where the village of Cannae lay is not stated, so the village is not drawn. The paths of the cavalry are drawn straight; the accounts do not give their routes.

phases.title: The armies draw up facing each other
phases.text: The Romans faced east with the Aufidus on their right and massed their infantry deep in the centre. Hannibal put the Hispanic and Gallic infantry in the middle, the African infantry at the ends of the infantry line and the cavalry on the flanks.
phases.quote: The Romans followed this convention fairly closely, but chose extra depth rather than breadth for the infantry in hopes of breaking quickly through the center of Hannibal's line.

phases.title: The cavalry clash and the centres advance
phases.text: The battle opened with a fierce cavalry fight on both flanks. In the centre Hannibal moved the Hispanic and Gallic infantry forward in a curve, keeping the Africans back.
phases.quote: The battle began with a fierce cavalry engagement on the flanks.

phases.title: The Roman cavalry is driven off
phases.text: The Carthaginian horse got the upper hand on the Roman right. Hasdrubal did not chase them but rode to the other side of the field, and the allied cavalry broke between him and the Numidians.
phases.quote: Instead, he led them to the other side of the field to attack the socii cavalry still fighting the Numidians.

phases.title: The centre gives way step by step
phases.text: The Roman heavy infantry pressed forward and Hannibal held his men together in a controlled retreat. The curve buckled inwards as the Romans advanced and reserve lines pushed into the gaps.
phases.quote: The crescent of Hispanic and Gallic troops buckled inwards as they gradually withdrew step by step.

phases.title: The Africans turn in and the cavalry takes the rear
phases.text: The Carthaginian cavalry attacked the Roman centre from behind. Hannibal then ordered the African infantry to turn inwards against the Roman flanks, which formed a pincer.
phases.quote: At this decisive point, Hannibal ordered his African infantry to turn inwards and advance against the Roman flanks, creating an encirclement in one of the earliest known examples of a pincer movement.

phases.title: The Romans are enclosed and killed
phases.text: Enclosed in a pocket with no means of escape, the Roman infantry was cut down by the cavalry behind it, the African infantry on both sides and the centre in front.
phases.quote: The Romans were henceforth enclosed in a pocket with no means of escape. The Carthaginians created a wall and began to systematically massacre them.
